title: Manuscript annotation
description: A thought the author had while reading a specific passage (conventions §14). Anchored to prose, not to canon. Distinct from material: material is an idea that may enter the story; an annotation is a reaction to what is already on the page.

anchor.description: What the note is about. A passage note carries scene, paragraph and quote — resolved in that order of durability. A scene note carries the scene alone: it is about the section rather than a sentence in it, which is the only shape an observation about something ABSENT can take, since absent text cannot be quoted. A scene note can never drift and never orphan; only deleting the scene breaks it.

paragraph.description: 0-based paragraph index when the note was made. Absent means the note is about the whole scene.

quote.description: The selected text, verbatim — the durable fallback when indices shift. Requires a paragraph: a quote with no index is an incoherent anchor, not a scene note.

paragraphs.description: The verbatim text of each paragraph the note covers, captured when the note was made — the note's own record of what it was talking about, because paragraphs change over time. One entry for a plain passage note; several, in order, when the quote spans further. Display and learning context, never a resolution key: resolution still follows the quote. Requires a paragraph for the same reason a quote does — a scene note's referent is the scene, which needs no snapshot.

body.description: The note itself, in the author's words. Never categorised by them.

kind.description: Absent or `note` is a thought with a status lifecycle. `keypoint` is a margin-timeline marker — a structural statement of what a passage must get across, never a request for change. A keypoint has no lifecycle: it exists or it does not, which is why it carries no status.

by.description: Who made it. Keypoints minted by a session are always `by: agent`, so the author can read the trail as the proposal it is.

status.description: A note's lifecycle. Required on a note; refused on a keypoint — giving a keypoint a status would put a structural marker into every surface that works notes as tasks.

links.description: What this note became when its scope outgrew the passage — material, obligation, or canon ids.

then.description: A keypoint carries no status. The backend never writes one, and the arc-canon skill §11 instructs sessions not to — so a keypoint that has acquired one is a marker that has drifted into being a task, which is exactly the confusion the two kinds exist to keep apart.

else.description: A note is a thought, and a thought has a lifecycle.
